election._note: By law no later than September 2029, no fixed date announced; Wikipedia 'Next Austrian legislative election'

dissolution._note: The Nationalrat dissolves itself by simple law before its term expires -- the mechanism actually used. The Federal President can also dissolve it on the government's proposal, but only once for the same reason, and has done so only once in the Republic's history (1930); constitutional convention treats that power as effectively dead. Neither is an executive command the player can issue, so this refuses. parlament.gv.at, 'The Federal President'; Wikipedia, 'Self-elimination of the Austrian Parliament'.

head_of_state._note: The Bundespräsident, popularly elected for a six-year term; last elected October 2022, so the next is due October 2028. Ceremonial -- no reader beyond the government panel. Wikipedia, 'President of Austria'.
head_of_state.title: Federal President
head_of_state.name: Elisabeth Kranzler

amendment._note: Art. 44: an ordinary constitutional amendment needs a 2/3 majority of the Nationalrat with at least half its members present. A total revision additionally requires a referendum -- not modelled, since no amendment content in this game rewrites the whole constitution. parlament.gv.at, 'Legislative process'.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: The 1919 Habsburg Law and the republic's own constitutional practice treat the republican form as excluded from ordinary revision -- a thinner citation than France's Art. 89 §5 or Germany's Art. 79(3) eternity clause, flagged as such rather than asserted with equal confidence.

formation._note: Chancellor appointed by the Federal President. A majority of the Nationalrat can topple the Federal Government at any time; a minority government survives only while tolerated. parlament.gv.at 'Vote of no confidence'.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 20% is Austria's own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Corporate 23% is Austria's own statutory rate, reduced from 25% in 2024 (BMF). Income is France's 20 scaled by Austria's OECD Revenue Statistics personal-tax-to-GDP share against France's, landing close to France's own at 19. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 55.2% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
